description: Opus 5.5 held-out run: the first stage of a Finnish agent participle. Its Tier-3 degree-modification bracket at step 8 once hung below syntax that appears later in the stage, about 1,250 px under its two words and off the canvas.
source: Claude Opus 5.5, high effort, Anthropic qualification run heldout-20261029/h1-084-fi-agent-participle, analysis 1. Exact copy of the response analysis. Saved in ~/Library/Application Support/Babel/anthropic-qualification/heldout-20261029/runs/h1-084-fi-agent-participle.
sentence: Luulen, että Pekan ostama auto on liian kallis.

derivationStages.statement: The predicative adjective phrase 'liian kallis' is built.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The adjective 'kallis' projects to A', and the degree word 'liian' projects its own DegP, which is merged as the specifier of the adjective phrase. The degree-modification relation connects the DegP to the A' it modifies, so 'liian' scales the excessiveness of 'kallis' rather than modifying the clause.

derivationStages.statement: The copula 'on' takes the AP as its complement.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The copular verb 'on' is merged with the adjective phrase, which forms V' and then VP. The complement-selection relation records that the copula selects the predicative AP as its complement. The copula assigns no theta role of its own; the AP is the semantic predicate of the embedded clause.

derivationStages.statement: Inside the participial relative, the verb 'osta' takes a null operator as its object.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A separate object is started for the agent-participle modifier. The verb stem 'osta' ('buy') is merged with a silent relative operator in object position, which forms V' and VP. The theta-assignment relation records that 'osta' assigns the Theme role to the operator. The operator, not the noun 'auto', fills the gap, because 'auto' is the head of the containing noun phrase.

derivationStages.statement: The agent-participle head '-ma' projects PartP, and the genitive agent 'Pekan' is its specifier.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The participial head '-ma' takes the VP as its complement, which forms Part'. The proper noun 'Pekan' projects N' and NP, and this NP is merged as the specifier of PartP. Two relations follow, in this order. First, the participial predicate Part' assigns the Agent role to 'Pekan'. Second, the agent-participle head '-ma' licenses genitive case on that specifier. The genitive is the case that Finnish agent participles assign to their agent.

derivationStages.statement: The verb 'osta' raises to the participial head and yields 'ostama'.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The verb stem 'osta' moves out of VP and adjoins to the participial head '-ma', which creates a complex Part head. It leaves a trace in its base position inside V'. The head-movement relation links the raised verb, its trace and the host head. This movement is why the stem surfaces fused with the suffix as 'ostama'.

derivationStages.statement: A null complementizer closes the reduced relative, and the operator moves to its specifier.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent relative complementizer is merged with PartP, which forms C'. The null operator then moves from object position to the specifier of this CP and leaves a trace behind. The operator-movement relation links the operator at the clause edge to its trace. The resulting operator-variable chain lets the gap be interpreted as the thing Pekka bought.

derivationStages.statement: The relative CP adjoins to N' of 'auto', which forms the embedded subject NP 'Pekan ostama auto'.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The noun 'auto' projects N'. The relative CP left-adjoins to that N', which creates a higher N' segment, and the NP is completed. The predication link coindexes the null operator with the N' of 'auto'. By this link the head noun is identified as the bought object, so the phrase means 'the car that Pekka bought'.

derivationStages.statement: The finite embedded IP is built, with 'Pekan ostama auto' as its subject.
derivationStages.stageRecord: An abstract finite present-tense I takes the copular VP as its complement, which forms I'. The subject NP is merged in the specifier of IP. Three relations follow, in this order. First, the subject is predicated of the copular VP, so the car is what is too expensive. Second, finite I assigns nominative case to the subject. Third, I agrees with the subject in third person singular, which the copula 'on' reflects.

derivationStages.statement: The copula 'on' raises from V to the finite I.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The finite copula moves from V and adjoins to the abstract finite I, which forms a complex I head. It leaves a trace before the AP. The head-movement relation links the raised copula, its trace and the I host. Through this movement the copula carries the tense and agreement features of I.

derivationStages.statement: The complementizer 'että' heads the embedded CP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The declarative complementizer 'että' is merged with the finite IP, which forms C' and CP. The complement-selection relation records that 'että' selects a finite IP complement.

derivationStages.statement: The matrix verb 'luule' takes the että-clause as its internal argument.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The verb stem 'luule' ('think') is merged with the embedded CP, which forms V' and VP. The theta-assignment relation records that 'luule' assigns its internal Proposition role to the että-clause.

derivationStages.statement: The matrix IP is built, with first-person agreement '-n' in I and a null pro subject.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The finite I bearing the first-person singular ending '-n' takes the matrix VP, which forms I'. A silent pronominal subject is merged in the specifier of IP. Four relations follow, in this order. First, the VP assigns the Experiencer role to pro. Second, finite I assigns nominative case to pro. Third, I agrees with pro in first person singular. Fourth, this rich agreement identifies the content of pro, which licenses the subject drop that Finnish allows in the first person.

derivationStages.statement: The matrix verb raises to I and surfaces as 'luulen', which completes the sentence.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The verb stem 'luule' moves from V and adjoins to the finite I '-n', which forms a complex I head. It leaves a trace before the embedded clause. The head-movement relation links the raised verb, its trace and the agreement host. The movement accounts for the inflected form 'luulen' preceding 'että', and it yields the final structure of the sentence.
